facts.raw_span: pruritic, pink scaling plaques on her face and neck
lesions subsequently involved her chest, abdomen, and back and flared with sun exposure
Well-demarcated plaques with an overlying scale crust occurring in a photodistributed pattern on the central face, with involvement of chest, abdomen, and back
Antinuclear antibody titers positive at 1:640
Lymphopenia present
Normocytic anemia present
Epidermal acanthosis, spongiosis, and acantholytic keratinocytes
Dense lymphoplasmacellular infiltrate in the dermis, with scattered neutrophils and eosinophils
Granular and linear deposition of IgG and C3 at the basement membrane zone and abundant intercellular deposition of IgG and C3 in the upper two-thirds of the epidermis
Negative or within normal limits: antiribonucleoprotein, antihistone, antiphospholipid, anti-Smith, anti-Ro/Sjögren syndrome antigen A, and anti-La/Sjögren syndrome antigen B antibodies
Normal C3, C4, CH50, rapid plasma reagin, and creatinine levels
Normal erythrocyte sedimentation rate

concepts.why: The patient's positive antinuclear antibody titers, epidermal acanthosis, and granular deposition of IgG and C3 at the basement membrane zone are consistent with lupus erythematosus.
The patient's pruritic, pink scaling plaques, lesions involving the chest, abdomen, and back, and photodistributed pattern are consistent with subacute cutaneous lupus erythematosus.
The patient's well-demarcated plaques with an overlying scale crust, epidermal acanthosis, and dense lymphoplasmacellular infiltrate in the dermis are consistent with discoid lupus erythematosus.

The patient's epidermal acanthosis, spongiosis, and acantholytic keratinocytes, as well as the granular deposition of IgG and C3 at the basement membrane zone, are consistent with pemphigus foliaceus.

The patient's pruritic, pink scaling plaques, lesions involving the chest, abdomen, and back, and photodistributed pattern, as well as the epidermal acanthosis and spongiosis, are consistent with pemphigus erythematosus.

rationales.F01: Pruritic, pink scaling plaques are common in various skin conditions, but the presence of these symptoms suggests an autoimmune or inflammatory process.
rationales.F02: Lesions that flare with sun exposure are characteristic of subacute cutaneous lupus erythematosus.
rationales.F04: High antinuclear antibody titers are a strong indicator of lupus erythematosus.
rationales.F07: Epidermal acanthosis, spongiosis, and acantholytic keratinocytes are histopathological features of pemphigus foliaceus.
rationales.F09: Granular and linear deposition of IgG and C3 at the basement membrane zone is a characteristic finding in lupus erythematosus.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's presentation of pruritic, pink scaling plaques that flare with sun exposure, along with positive antinuclear antibody titers and specific histopathological findings, supports the diagnosis of Subacute cutaneous lupus erythematosus, which is a subtype of Lupus erythematosus.
